content: In run-20260803-riskband-001, the live Architect dispatch returned findings wrapped in a Markdown code fence, violating architect.md's no-fence Output contract; harness/orchestrator/core.py's no-fence-stripping policy required treating this as a parse failure and blocking Research rather than silently repairing the response.

In this environment, OBSIDIAN_VAULT_PATH remains unset; a real in-pipeline Architect mcp__obsidian__read_note call for 'Harness Run Summaries/run-summary-run-20260908-obsidianlive-001.md' (run-20260916-hardfailbound-001, Research phase) returned connector_unavailable, and the orchestrator's retain_architect_obsidian_reads bridge correctly retained that negative observation (classified not_applicable) without performing an independent re-read or manufacturing a verified read.

engineer.md documents an explicit 'Command grammar' contract for requested_command.command but does not explicitly state that working_directory must be a relative path; the real test-runner Skill wrapper rejects an absolute or drive-prefixed working_directory (rejection_category: request_value_invalid). A live Engineer dispatch (agent abe70f4eef319978b, run-20260917-logicrepair-001, task T-LOGICREPAIR-DEMO) supplied an absolute Windows path as working_directory for its C-1 pre_test_requested command, and the wrapper correctly rejected it, halting Implementation before any test ran.

live_cli.py's promote_artifact operation has no distinctly-named-path parameter for the four canonical phase artifacts -- evidence_io.CANONICAL_FILENAMES is a fixed phase->filename map with no override, so it always writes to the plain canonical name (e.g. verification-report.json) and refuses (EvidenceCollisionError) if that path already exists. work/SKILL.md's 'Same-run logic-failure route-back to the Engineer' section documents promoting a repair round's artifacts to a distinctly-named path (e.g. implementation-report.repair-1.json / verification-report.repair-1.json), but this convention cannot currently be executed through the live bridge as implemented -- confirmed by a real EvidenceCollisionError when run-20260917-logicrepair-002's resumed process attempted to promote a second verification-report.json.

The test-runner wrapper (.claude/skills/test-runner/scripts/run_command.py) requires a request file's basename (minus .json) to exactly equal the JSON body's own command_id field -- both an embedded dot (e.g. 'V-1.resume2') and a basename/body mismatch (e.g. filename 'V-1-resume2' with body command_id 'V-1') are rejected (rejection_category identifier_invalid / request_path_identifier_mismatch respectively) before any real command runs. Confirmed live in run-20260917-logicrepair-002 with two real command_rejected responses.

The production fix for the artifact-promotion gap (evidence_io.repair_artifact_filename; live_cli.py op_promote_artifact's new repair_attempt field, bounded by core.MAX_LOGIC_REPAIR_ATTEMPTS) works live: run-20260918-logicrepair-003 genuinely promoted implementation-report.repair-1.json and verification-report.repair-1.json through the real live bridge (not core.py's deterministic fakes), closing the same-run logic-repair route-back loop end-to-end for the first time with real dispatched Architect/Engineer/Quality-Engineer agents and a genuine final_verdict: pass.

T-FLAKY-DEMO / run-20260919-flaky-001 genuinely completed ASSIGNMENT.md's planted-flaky-test acceptance criterion live end-to-end, closing the remaining_risk left open by run-20260918-logicrepair-003 ('Plan and execute the separate flaky-test infrastructure-flake demonstration milestone'). The Quality Engineer's first real attempt against demo-repo/tests/integration/test_calibration_feed_connectivity.py (V-2) genuinely failed with a named ConnectionResetError from a one-shot marker-file-backed cold-start simulation, was classified infrastructure_flake on that concrete evidence, and an identical retry (V-3, within retry_policy.max_retries: 2) genuinely passed -- routed_back_to_engineer.routed is false, confirming a genuine transient failure was never misrouted to the Engineer as a logic_bug. The process that reached this state was interrupted before run-summary.json was written; the checkpoint (status: complete, next_resume_action: null) and full retained evidence (attempts, logs, verification-report.json, policy-events.jsonl, flaky-sentinel/state.json showing attempted: true) were independently audited and found fully self-consistent, so the terminal artifacts were finished from that evidence rather than by re-running verification or re-triggering the already-consumed one-shot flake.

run-20260929-costproof-001 (T-COSTPROOF) completed all four phases (Discovery/Research/Implementation/Verification) end-to-end with a genuine final_verdict: pass and zero transport_parse_failure policy events across 21 retained policy events -- the same Percentage.__post_init__ validation fix that run-20260929-percentage-001's Engineer produced correctly but could not deliver (blocked by two independent transport-contract violations within one Implementation phase, see FACT-20260929-ENGINEER-DOUBLE-TRANSPORT-FAILURE). The only procedural difference in this run's Agent/SendMessage dispatch prompts was appending an explicit reminder sentence restating the raw-JSON, no-fence, no-prose output contract to every dispatch and every SendMessage reply (per this run's own explicit orchestrator instruction) -- every staged turn from the Architect, Engineer, and Quality Engineer parsed as strict JSON on the first attempt.
